newsitem.title: USA: Texas rivers turn deadly after heavy rains.
newsitem.headline: Texas rivers turn deadly after heavy rains.

text.p: Heavy rains turned several Texas rivers into raging torrents Tuesday that killed one person and forced the closure of many highways, officials said.
As much as a foot of rain fell in parts of central and southwestern Texas Monday and Tuesday, rapidly filling lakes and rivers depleted by a blistering summer drought.

Texas Department of Public Safety spokeswoman Sherri Deatherage Green said Charles Leroy Connel, 66, was found dead after his pickup truck was washed down the rain-swollen Nueces River near Barksdale, Texas, 95 miles west of San Antonio.

Edwards County Judge Nevil Smart said many people got trapped in their cars when they tried to cross low-water bridges swept by rushing rivers in the rugged ranch country west of San Antonio, but that U.S. Border Patrol helicopters had been used to rescue them.
"The rain fell so fast and so hard, it didn't have any place to go. The rivers were way out of their banks," Smart said.
The Colorado River north of Austin rose so quickly that several houseboats got pulled from their moorings and washed downriver, police said.

Lake Travis, a 70-mile-long lake on the Colorado, was 20 feet below normal levels before the rains because of the summer's extended drought. But officials of the Lower Colorado River Authority said it was rising a foot an hour and would be just a few feet below normal by Wednesday.
Despite the flooding, only one home was reported damaged by water, said Deatherage Green.
